ranking.note: Kept P1; placed ahead of #10102 because it is the stated prerequisite and must be reviewed first in the chain.
Raised to P2: it is an explicit architectural prerequisite for running indexes out of process (#10102) and removes cs_main contention, so it cannot sit below the P3 test/build items it enables.
Lowered to P4: superseded by #35037, which solves the same FD-exhaustion problem with the per-address design reviewers preferred; redundant work, not a separate problem.

inconsistencies: #34978 and #35037 address the same file-descriptor accounting problem for IPC listeners; #35037 is the agreed successor and should be reviewed first, with #34978 only revisited if #35037 stalls.

Dependency chain that fixes review order: #29409 (Chain capnp wrapper) → #10102 (multiprocess split) → #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) → #19461 (bitcoin-gui -ipcconnect). Reviewing the later links in isolation is of little use; #19461 contains only one new commit on top of the rest.
#36190 tests behaviour introduced by #36105; #36105 must land or at least be agreed first, otherwise the test has nothing to assert.

#32387 (Windows IPC), #35932 (disconnect drain) and #36097 (cancellation arguments) all carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits pending upstream PRs (#335, #342); they will conflict in the subtree and should be sequenced rather than reviewed as independent patches.

#30437 (bitcoin-mine test program) and #36097 (cancellation on mining calls) both shape how external mining clients drive the IPC mining interface; deciding the cancellation pattern in #36097 may change the example client in #30437.
result.notes: Band spread reflects the category's stated ordering: the process-separation chain and the shutdown crash fix are P1; platform coverage, connection-resource safety, external-miner enablement and the wallet/GUI separation steps are P2; wrapper bug fixes, build guards and test/fuzz coverage are P3. Draft status, failing CI and rebase needs (noted on #32387, #35932, #36060, #24230) were ignored for banding.
